edgecore-mesa-az.name: EdgeCore Mesa Data Center Campus
edgecore-mesa-az.water_notes: Air-cooled design requires no water recharge; closed-loop chilled water system
edgecore-mesa-az.source: EdgeCore Announces Metro Phoenix Expansion to 450MW
edgecore-mesa-az.notes: Elliot Road Technology Corridor, Mesa. CEO stated 'Greater Phoenix is fast becoming the AI center of the West.' Expansion land purchase adds 43.87 acres to 40-acre original site. EdgeCore raised $2B equity and $2B debt in 2024. Coordinates approximate for Elliot Road corridor. Arizona's data-center sales/use-tax exemption (A.R.S. Sec. 41-1519) applies by statute, but no campus-specific certified award was publicly verifiable (eligibility != confirmed award); the $150M cited is first-building capex and the $2B equity + $2B debt EdgeCore raised in 2024 is corporate financing, not Mesa-campus capex.

google-redhawk-mesa-az.name: Google Redhawk Mesa Data Center Campus
google-redhawk-mesa-az.water_notes: Google built the Mesa campus as air-cooled, chosen for Arizona's watershed scarcity; Mesa's economic-development director described it at groundbreaking as a 'cutting-edge, air-cooled data center campus.' The 2019 City of Mesa development agreement separately provided for the city to supply up to ~1 million gallons/day at launch, scaling toward ~4 million gallons/day at full build-out — a contractual water allocation/backup (on-site storage, existing wells, acquired water rights, long-term storage credits), not confirmed operational cooling consumption. No operational water-use figure has been published.
google-redhawk-mesa-az.source: Google breaks ground on Mesa data center campus in Arizona
google-redhawk-mesa-az.notes: Three-phase campus through 2030; originally filed anonymously as Project Red Hawk via LLC Stone Applications. Phase 1 operational July 2025. Phase 2 under construction. Coordinates at Elliot and Sossaman roads, SE Mesa. 2019 development agreement requires >=$600M capex by 2025, >=$1B by 2029, 750,000 sq ft built by 2030, and a >=$65,000 average full-time data-center salary; construction workforce has been cited around 1,200 (an estimate, not a permanent-jobs count).

meta-mesa-az.name: Meta Mesa Data Center
meta-mesa-az.source: Mesa, we are online! — Meta's Mesa data center serving traffic (Jan 2025), $1B+ in Arizona
meta-mesa-az.notes: Meta data center at 3841 S Ellsworth Rd in the Elliot Road Technology Corridor, Mesa, Maricopa County — land acquired 2021 (shell entity 'Redale LLC'), came online in 2025, and was redesigned for AI workloads during construction (baxtel). Meta states 'more than $1 billion' invested in Arizona. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the disclosed Ellsworth Rd address; a county-parcel pass could upgrade precision to exact.

ntt-global-mesa-az.name: NTT Global Data Centers Mesa — Pacific Proving Technology Park
ntt-global-mesa-az.water_notes: Closed-loop cooling proposed; community activists cite Arizona drought and Colorado River water stress
ntt-global-mesa-az.source: NTT acquires 173-acre planned data center park in Mesa for $300m
ntt-global-mesa-az.notes: investmentUsd is $300M land purchase only; total buildout investment is substantially higher. NE corner of Pecos and Crismon roads, far SE Mesa. Seven two-story buildings totaling 1.7M sq ft + warehouse + office. NTT's second Phoenix-area campus (existing 102-acre, 240MW campus is ~4 miles north on Elliot Road). Phase 1 targeted November 2028. Coordinates approximate for Pecos/Crismon intersection.

prologis-stem-park-zanker-road-san-jose-.name: Prologis STEM Park
prologis-stem-park-zanker-road-san-jose-.source: 400MW Prologis data center campus chosen as preferred project on city-owned land in San Jose, California
prologis-stem-park-zanker-road-san-jose-.notes: 159-acre city-owned parcel at Hwy 237 & Zanker Road, North San Jose (bounded by Los Esteros Energy Center, Artesian Slough, Hwy 237, and the Silicon Valley Advanced Water Purification Center). Prologis selected as preferred developer by San Jose City Council (unanimous vote, Nov 18 2025) over Catellus-Deca and Trammell Crow proposals; CEQA review and ground-lease negotiation still pending as of source dates — not yet approved. 'STEM Park' = Sustainable Technology, Engineering and Manufacturing Park: four 99MW data-center buildings (1.68M sq ft total, capacityMw above) plus a separate ~785,000 sq ft / 100MW advanced-manufacturing component (not counted in capacityMw, different use). PG&E has committed initial 250MW via dual feed from the Los Esteros 230kV substation within 30-36 months. ~$25B investment widely reported (DCD et al.) but not confirmed directly by Prologis — omitted from investmentUsd. Projected 6,000+ jobs and $30M/yr city tax revenue are projections tied to a not-yet-approved project, not delivered counts — omitted from jobs numeric. A separate, already-tracked Prologis site (prologis-silver-creek-valley-san-jose-ca) and another new Prologis San Jose site (prologis-rue-ferrari-san-jose-ca, this same batch) are distinct parcels, not duplicates.

starwood-digital-project-washington-de.name: Project Washington (Starwood Digital Ventures)
starwood-digital-project-washington-de.water_notes: Starwood states the campus would use about 12.7 million gallons of water per year at full build-out, with a one-time ~600,000-gallon fill for its closed-loop cooling system; the regulatory filing cited a broader range of roughly 9.9-20 million gallons/year, and reviewers questioned whether that is low for a 1.2 GW campus.
starwood-digital-project-washington-de.source: Delaware City data center faces major setback after environmental denial
starwood-digital-project-washington-de.notes: Largest proposed data center in Delaware history. 11 two-story buildings, 5 substations, 1 switch station, 516 emergency diesel generators on 580 acres. CZA permit denied February 4, 2026; denial unanimously upheld by Coastal Zone Industrial Control Board March 26, 2026. Appeal to Delaware Superior Court anticipated. Delaware Building Trades Council exclusive union labor agreement in place. Original $9.7B investment figure removed — not confirmed in any cited source. Coordinates approximate for Delaware City area.

dc-blox-atlanta-west-ga.name: DC BLOX Atlanta West (ATL1)
dc-blox-atlanta-west-ga.water_notes: DC BLOX's campus design specifies high-efficiency magnetic-bearing air-cooled chillers with thermal storage and provisions for a future liquid-cooling tie-in (operator campus page); the company characterizes the design as effectively waterless. Air-cooled chillers still use minimal water (humidification/occasional evaporative assist); no quantified water-use (MGD) figure has been published, and use could change if the liquid-cooling provision is activated.
dc-blox-atlanta-west-ga.source: DC BLOX Secures $1.15 Billion Green Loan for Atlanta Data Center Campus Development
dc-blox-atlanta-west-ga.notes: Initial 120 MW phase (Building A); site plan includes additional 80 MW Building B (delivery early 2028) and 80 MW Building C (early 2029) totaling 200+ MW. investmentUsd reflects green loan construction financing announced August 11, 2025. Located adjacent to Microsoft Douglasville campus, 2.5 miles from Google facility. Coordinates are Lithia Springs area centroid. Original DCD source URL returned HTTP 404 and was replaced with the DC BLOX official press release, which resolves and supports all claims. The $98M Douglasville abatement was granted for the campus in the Riverside West Business Park (New River Road); city/authority filings cite 25 permanent jobs (~$130k average) and up to 500 construction jobs over five years — projections, not confirmed headcounts.

apple-waukee-ia.name: Apple Waukee Data Center
apple-waukee-ia.source: Seven years on, Iowa's Apple data center finally opens — $1.3B, 2,000 acres, first building operational Oct 2024, announced 2017
apple-waukee-ia.notes: Apple data center near the intersection of Hickman Rd and S Avenue, Waukee, Dallas County — announced by Tim Cook in 2017; first building became operational in October 2024 on a 2,000-acre site, a $1.3B investment (AppleInsider). Apple's Feb 2025 newsroom names Iowa among states for continued data-center capacity expansion. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are an approximate geocode; a county-parcel pass could upgrade precision to exact.

t5-chicago-iv-grayslake-il.name: T5 Chicago IV (CHI IV)
t5-chicago-iv-grayslake-il.source: T5 plans five gigawatt-scale data center campuses, announces Chicago campus
t5-chicago-iv-grayslake-il.notes: CHI IV in Grayslake, Lake County (~40 mi north of Chicago): up to 1.2 GW IT capacity with 1.6 GW secured ComEd power; envisions 20 × 60 MW buildings, Phase 1 (3 × 60 MW) targeted Q4 2027. Recorded as proposed (announced; no groundbreaking confirmed). Distinct from T5's Palmetto, GA campus. Coordinates are the Grayslake area centroid.

amazon-project-rainier-new-carlisle-in.name: Amazon Project Rainier
amazon-project-rainier-new-carlisle-in.water_notes: Outside-air (free) cooling for roughly 98% of operating hours, running essentially chiller-free. 1.58 MGD is the Phase 1 permitted cooling-water discharge cap (average discharge ~0.8 MGD). Full-campus water use is not publicly disclosed by AWS; residents have raised aquifer-withdrawal concerns.
amazon-project-rainier-new-carlisle-in.source: Amazon opens $11B AI data center Project Rainier in Indiana — CNBC

google-project-louie-monrovia-in.name: Google Project Louie (Morgan County)
google-project-louie-monrovia-in.water_notes: Each building estimated to use up to 4 million gallons per day at maximum capacity per IURC filings; total campus water demand not confirmed as a single figure. Cooling type not confirmed in available sources.
google-project-louie-monrovia-in.source: Google behind 390-acre data center development in Morgan County, Indiana
google-project-louie-monrovia-in.notes: Codename 'Project Louie'; Google initially concealed via shell company 'Woodland Caribou LLC'. Campus totals approximately 550 acres in Morgan Township east of Monrovia (bounded by Keller Hill Rd, N Antioch Rd, SR-42, W Union Church Rd); additional ~80 acres acquired within Monrovia town limits, bringing total Google holdings to ~628 acres. Planned 1,200 MW AES Indiana substation per IURC Cause No. 46394 (filed Apr 22 2026); that figure is the utility substation capacity ceiling, not a confirmed steady-state data center load — treated as notes per spec. Six buildings plus substation planned. Reported total investment ~$1 billion (IDS News; not confirmed as a firm Google-stated commitment — left out of investmentUsd). Land acquisition spend: ~$78 million for ~15 parcels Sep–Nov 2025. Coordinates approximate (site east of Monrovia near SR-42/Keller Hill Rd area). Annexation dispute with Town of Monrovia active July 2026: county transferred Google parcels to RDC under IC 36-4-3-4.3 to block annexation; Google offered $12M sewer plant upgrade to Monrovia to drop the effort.

project-shirley-eagle-creek-township-lak.name: Project Shirley
project-shirley-eagle-creek-township-lak.source: In Indiana, an anatomy of data center opposition
project-shirley-eagle-creek-township-lak.notes: Unincorporated, SR-2/Clay St. 4 buildings across 160 largely agricultural acres. Coordinates are approximate.

terawulf-hawesville-ky.name: Justified Data Campus
terawulf-hawesville-ky.water_notes: TeraWulf stated at community meetings that no river water or municipal water will be used. Advanced closed-loop liquid cooling system; company stated campus will use less water over several years than the former aluminum smelter consumed in a single day. No reported MGD figure available.
terawulf-hawesville-ky.source: TeraWulf Announces Anthropic Lease at Justified Data Campus
terawulf-hawesville-ky.notes: Brownfield redevelopment of former Century Aluminum smelter. Site acquired February 2026 from Century Aluminum subsidiary; acquisition price reported by multiple outlets as $200M cash plus a 6.8% minority equity interest in TeraWulf (not confirmed in official PR text fetched). Lease entity: TeraWulf's Raylan Data LLC to Anthropic PBC. The ~$19B is contracted lease revenue over the 20-year term — not capex; excluded from investmentUsd. TeraWulf indicated a $3B–$4B construction investment for two data center buildings (range, not a firm single figure; excluded from investmentUsd). Site has ~480 MW of existing power availability; 401 MW is the Anthropic lease capacity. Total site ~750 acres per news sources; TeraWulf's official PR cited 'over 250 buildable acres.' Coordinates are approximate (Hawesville town center). Fluidstack/Abernathy JV is a separate unrelated transaction — excluded from this record.

terawulf-muskie-eastpark-ky.name: TeraWulf Muskie Data Campus (EastPark)
terawulf-muskie-eastpark-ky.source: New AI data center coming to eastern Kentucky
terawulf-muskie-eastpark-ky.notes: TeraWulf's second Kentucky campus (alongside the Justified/Hawesville campus tracked separately). TeraWulf (Nasdaq: WULF), historically a bitcoin miner, repositioning toward HPC/AI. Muskie is a 285-acre site at EastPark Industrial Park (a 1,000-acre former strip mine). Planned 1+ GW phased: initial 500 MW ramp H2 2028, additional 500 MW targeted H2 2030. County discrepancy: local TV cites Boyd County, but Wikipedia and the Lane Report place EastPark primarily in Greenup County (site straddles Boyd/Greenup/Carter); Greenup used, city Ashland retained as the regional reference. INVESTMENT OMITTED: the $4B figure came from a Boyd County official, not TeraWulf's investor PR or 8-K. ~300 permanent jobs are official projections (in notes, not jobs). TeraWulf stated it will pay the full standard industrial tariff with no subsidies. Coordinates are the EastPark park centroid.

stack-caddo-parish-la.name: Caddo Parish Campus (with Amazon)
stack-caddo-parish-la.source: Campuses of newly-announced Amazon data center spanning Bossier, Caddo parishes confirmed
stack-caddo-parish-la.notes: Part of a ~$12,000,000,000 combined Amazon/STACK investment spanning this Caddo Parish campus and the companion Bossier Parish campus (Benton, LA).

mghpcc-holyoke-ma.name: Massachusetts Green High Performance Computing Center
mghpcc-holyoke-ma.source: Massachusetts Green High Performance Computing Center
mghpcc-holyoke-ma.notes: 90,300 sq ft, opened 2012, hydro-powered university research-computing consortium (100 Bigelow St). Explicitly exempted from Holyoke's 2026 data center ban. Houses the MIT Lincoln Laboratory Supercomputing Center (LLSC / TX-GAIA) — recorded as one facility, not two.

sentinel-jay-me.name: Sentinel Data Centers Androscoggin Mill Campus, Jay
sentinel-jay-me.powered_by: On-site solar (up to 150MW), Central Maine Power (up to 25MW backup), on-site hydro approved
sentinel-jay-me.water_notes: Closed-loop system; ~300,000 gallons/day from Androscoggin River to replace evaporation, compared to 35-40 million gallons/day used by former paper mill.
sentinel-jay-me.source: Jay Approves Town Meeting Warrant, Backs Data Center Plan
sentinel-jay-me.notes: Sentinel Data Centers LLC is headquartered in New York City. JGT2 Redevelopment purchased the former Pixelle Specialty Solutions mill in December 2023. ~425,000 sq ft of obsolete mill buildings demolished; paper machines shipped to Pakistan. In June 2026 Sentinel notified JGT2 of intent not to move forward; no permits were issued and no groundbreaking was held. JGT2 is seeking other operators for the site.

geronimo-nobles-county-powered-data-park.name: Nobles County Powered Data Park
geronimo-nobles-county-powered-data-park.source: Minnesota's long-predicted data center boom is on shaky ground

meta-forest-city-nc.name: Meta Forest City Data Center
meta-forest-city-nc.source: Meta Forest City Data Center info sheet — broke ground 2010, $750M+ invested in North Carolina
meta-forest-city-nc.notes: Meta (Facebook) data center on Social Circle, Forest City, Rutherford County — broke ground 2010, operational ~2012, a multi-parcel campus (parcels owned by 'Andale LLC', a Meta subsidiary confirmed via Meta's SEC 10-K Exhibit 21.1 and the Menlo Park HQ mailing address), with a third facility announced 2015. Meta reports $750M+ invested in North Carolina; the 408 Social Circle parcel alone carries $176.9M assessed building value (built, not land-bank). No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are a Rutherford County GIS parcel centroid, held approximate pending a raw-geometry re-pull; a follow-up GIS pass could upgrade precision to exact.

project-delta-walnut-cove-nc.name: Project Delta Data Center – Stokes County
project-delta-walnut-cove-nc.utility: Duke Energy (Belews Creek proximity; no confirmed interconnection)
project-delta-walnut-cove-nc.water_notes: Developer estimates 50,000-100,000 gal/day (0.05-0.10 MGD) via a closed-loop system, sourced from municipal supply (not the Dan River) — a range, so no numeric MGD.
project-delta-walnut-cove-nc.source: NC communities push back on AI data centers – Project Delta lawsuit
project-delta-walnut-cove-nc.notes: Site on US Highway 311 and Tuttle Road near Belews Creek Coal Plant on Dan River. End operator/tenant not publicly identified; rezoning approved for unidentified operator per lawsuit. Rezoning voided April 14, 2026 after court challenge over statutory notice failures. Developer ELS plans to resubmit. Capacity and investment not disclosed. Coordinates are Walnut Cove city centroid.

drox-group-rural-hall-forsyth-county-nc.name: Rural Hall Data Center (The Drox Group)
drox-group-rural-hall-forsyth-county-nc.source: Planning board recommends denying rezoning for proposed Rural Hall data center
drox-group-rural-hall-forsyth-county-nc.notes: Coordinates are approximate for Rural Hall, NC.

aws-crosby-court-franklin-county-oh.name: AWS Crosby Court Campus
aws-crosby-court-franklin-county-oh.source: Franklin County Auditor parcel/GIS record (parcel 275-000010, 6685 Crosby Ct — VADATA INC, assessed building area 768,498 sq ft = built, 66.8 ac)
aws-crosby-court-franklin-county-oh.notes: Operational AWS data center on a ~67-acre Vadata Inc parcel at 6685 Crosby Ct, far-northwest Franklin County (Brown Township, Plain City mailing area, in the 'New California' growth corridor near the Union County line) — part of Amazon's AWS US-East-2 (Ohio) build-out. Franklin County Auditor assessed building area 768,498 sq ft (= built); owner Vadata Inc. The auditor land-use class here reads 'Other Industrial Research/Chemical Lab' rather than the 'data center' class used on the nearby Hilliard AWS parcels (an assessment-class quirk; the two Vadata parcels share an identical 768,498 sq ft building figure). Sits ~2 km south of the Amazon Warner Rd and Industrial Pkwy campuses across the line in Jerome Township, Union County. No dedicated second public source specific to 6685 Crosby Ct was found (a similarly-named baxtel 'Crosby Campus' entry documents a different New Albany site and was excluded); the record rests on the Franklin County Auditor parcel record. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are the Franklin County Auditor parcel centroid.

aws-3180-beech-road-new-albany-oh.name: AWS New Albany (3180 Beech Road)
aws-3180-beech-road-new-albany-oh.source: Licking County Auditor parcel/GIS record (parcel 095-111618-04.000, Beech Rd NW — Amazon Data Services Inc, Industrial land-use class 305 'Research/Chemical Labs' = built, 106.4 ac)
aws-3180-beech-road-new-albany-oh.notes: Operational AWS data center on a ~106-acre Amazon Data Services Inc parcel on Beech Rd NW, New Albany — a second built AWS building on Beech Rd, physically distinct from the tracked '2550 Beech Road' building (aws-2550-beech-road-new-albany-oh, ~1.1 km south) and from the under-construction ~458-acre Beech/Miller five-building expansion (aws-beech-road-new-albany-oh). Data-center directories label it the 'North Hub'; the 112-acre parcel was bought April 2020 for $21.8M and the building is listed as built 2024 / fully operational. Licking County Auditor land-use class 305 ('Research/Chemical Labs' = built industrial, vs class 300 'Industrial Vacant Land' on the neighboring pre-construction parcels); owner Amazon Data Services Inc. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are the Licking County Auditor parcel centroid (parcel 095-111618-04.000).

aws-galaxy-sidney-oh.name: AWS Project Galaxy — Sidney, OH
aws-galaxy-sidney-oh.water_notes: City of Sidney public water system (groundwater wells, Great Miami River, Tawawa Creek). Development agreement caps withdrawal at 1.0 million gallons per day (694 gpm maximum); projected average annual usage is 4.6 million gallons per year (~12,600 gpd average). All wastewater including cooling discharge routed to city sanitary sewer. Miami Valley Conservancy District raised concerns citing peak draw up to 300 gpm. Cooling type inferred from industrial-scale water-in / wastewater-out pattern; not explicitly stated in sources.
aws-galaxy-sidney-oh.source: Amazon secures tax break for $3bn data center campus in Sidney, Ohio
aws-galaxy-sidney-oh.notes: Codename 'Project Galaxy.' Coordinates approximate (parcel: north of Millcreek Road, west of Vandemark Road, Sidney OH). AES Ohio FERC filing shows phased power ramp: 65 MW at initial operations (Sept 15, 2026 target), 480 MW within one year, 1,500 MW by January 2031 — 1,500 MW taken as planned total capacity. $3B investment described as a firm commitment in the approved development agreement (not 'up to'). AWS has committed an estimated $23B in Ohio data centers through 2029–2030. Baxtel lists a 'West Hub' expansion site associated with this campus. FERC filing lists location as 'Jefferson Township, Ohio'; confirmed as Sidney/Shelby County campus from all other sources.

bristolville-25-lordstown-oh.name: Bristolville 25
bristolville-25-lordstown-oh.source: Data center developer taking Lordstown to court
bristolville-25-lordstown-oh.notes: 133 acres of industrial land near the former GM plant in Lordstown/Bristolville. The village enacted a data-center ban; the developer petitioned the Ohio Supreme Court for a writ of mandamus. Distinct from the already-tracked Stargate-Lordstown facility (different site/operator).

edgeconnex-mcn-new-albany-licking-county.name: EdgeConneX MCN New Albany (South Campus)
edgeconnex-mcn-new-albany-licking-county.source: Licking County parcel/GIS record (EdgeConneX MCN New Albany South PropCo 2 + North PropCo 1 parcels; anchor 9850 Innovation Campus Way, 33.86 ac, "Industrial Warehouses")
edgeconnex-mcn-new-albany-licking-county.notes: EdgeConneX's ~$1B multi-phase "MCN New Albany" South campus. Per the Ohio Tax Credit Authority scope-of-work filing: Phase I converts a ~525,000 sq ft existing warehouse (9850 Innovation Campus Way) into an 80 MW data center; Phase II proposes two new 72 MW facilities (144 MW) — capacityMw.planned = 224 (80 + 144, IT load). A co-located PowerConneX natural-gas energy center (reported 140–216 MW of generation across sources) is EXCLUDED from capacityMw as on-site generation, not IT load. Footprint spans the South PropCo 2 parcels (~97 ac incl. the built anchor) plus the adjacent North PropCo 1 parcel (3356 Clover Valley Rd NW, 170 ac); ~267 ac combined. "MCN" is EdgeConneX's internal project prefix (not publicly decoded). Distinct from EdgeConneX's separate Piper Farms parcel (~5 mi away) and from edgeconnex-ashville-oh (Pickaway County).

meta-middleton-township-oh.name: Meta Bowling Green (Project Accordion)
meta-middleton-township-oh.powered_by: Grid (100% renewable energy matching; Toledo Edison/FirstEnergy utility) plus 350 MW on-site gas generation (Will-Power Apollo facility, OPSB approved Feb 3, 2026)
meta-middleton-township-oh.source: Meta to develop data center campus outside Toledo, Ohio
meta-middleton-township-oh.notes: 715,000 sq ft facility on State Route 582 between SR-25 and I-75, Middleton Township, Wood County OH. Meta's 28th global and 2nd Ohio data center. The Apollo gas plant (OPSB Case No. 25-973-EL-BGN) operates behind-the-meter serving Liames LLC (Meta shell company); not grid-connected. Full capacity from Apollo expected late 2027. Coordinates are approximate Middleton Township centroid.

vantage-oh1-new-albany-licking-county-oh.name: Vantage Data Centers OH1
vantage-oh1-new-albany-licking-county-oh.source: Vantage Data Centers Breaks Ground on 192MW Campus, Enters Growing Ohio Data Center Market
vantage-oh1-new-albany-licking-county-oh.notes: 3325 Horizon Court, Johnstown — Licking County section of the New Albany International Business Park. Vantage's first Midwest campus and seventh North American market. 3 buildings, 1.5M+ sq ft total, 192MW total planned IT capacity (not yet fully operational). LEED Silver target, part of Vantage's 2030 net-zero operational carbon commitment. Vantage's own press release states OH1 "will provide secure and reliable infrastructure for cloud technologies and artificial intelligence" — real operator-stated AI-adjacent marketing (paired with "cloud," not an exclusive/GPU-specific claim), so tagged aiClassification: likely rather than confirmed.

beltline-oklahoma-city-frisco-road-ok.name: Beltline Energy Oklahoma City Campus
beltline-oklahoma-city-frisco-road-ok.source: Data center wins rezoning approval from OKC planning board
beltline-oklahoma-city-frisco-road-ok.notes: Two adjoining parcels rezoned via PUD cases likely numbered PUD-2105 (111.5 acres at 3025 N. Frisco Road, near I-40/Frisco Rd) and PUD-2124 (184 acres at 13921 NW 23rd Street, near NW 23rd/Frisco Rd, ~0.5 mi west of Yukon) — the case-number-to-address pairing is probable (inferred by matching geographic descriptors across sources) but not confirmed by a single primary document naming both together. OKC Planning Commission voted 7-0 to recommend approval Jan 21 2026; City Council final vote status is unconfirmed as of this writing (okc.gov council agendas were inaccessible during research) — treat as still-pending, not approved. Explicitly carved out of OKC's citywide data-center moratorium (~April 2026) as an already-pending application, confirming it remains active. Press coverage separately cites a larger '350-acre' and '480-acre' project total that doesn't reconcile with the confirmed 295.5-acre rezoned total (111.5+184) — the gap is plausibly an adjacent ~184.5-acre parcel Yukon Municipal Authority sold to BLE Landholdings LLC for $15.8M in Aug 2025 (near Hwy 66/Frisco Rd), which may be the same tract as the NW 23rd St parcel, but this is not confirmed. A $1B investment / 0.5GW capacity figure is associated with the broader Yukon-area BLE deal in local reporting but was not found tied specifically to this OKC rezoning by a primary source — omitted from capacityMw/investmentUsd pending confirmation rather than asserted.

google-muskogee-county-ok.name: Google Muskogee County Data Center Campuses
google-muskogee-county-ok.water_notes: Council Hill campus anticipates ~20,000 gal/day (~0.02 MGD, ~0.6% of Pryor's use) per Muskogee Rural Water District #3 vice-chair Howard Whatley — a forward estimate for a proposed facility (the low figure implies dry/air-based cooling, not confirmed). Summit campus water not disclosed.
google-muskogee-county-ok.source: Google to build two data centers in Muskogee County
google-muskogee-county-ok.notes: Two separate campuses near Summit and Council Hill in Muskogee County. Combined into one record; site-by-site capacity and investment breakdown not publicly available. Coordinates corrected to approximate Council Hill location (35.57°N, 95.65°W); original coordinates (35.65, −95.37) fell near Muskogee city / Summit area rather than Council Hill. Summit campus is located near Muskogee city (~17 miles east). Exact parcels not disclosed. Part of Google's $9B Oklahoma investment announced August 2025.

crane-pdx01-forest-grove-or.name: Crane PDX01
crane-pdx01-forest-grove-or.water_notes: Phase 1 confirmed air-based cooling (City Community Development Director; Crane CEO): the company 'has not applied to use water cooling for its first building ... will rely on air-based cooling, limiting water consumption to typical plumbing needs.' A 2023 release mentioned recycled water for cooling (likely a later phase).
crane-pdx01-forest-grove-or.source: Planning commission greenlights Crane DC's Forest Grove data center in northwest Oregon, again
crane-pdx01-forest-grove-or.notes: PDX01 data center campus in Forest Grove, Washington County; 76 MW by 2026. Coordinates are the Forest Grove area centroid. Development cost not disclosed (partner: Principal Asset Management) -> investmentUsd omitted. No job counts disclosed -> jobs honest-zero. Crane markets property-tax / enterprise-zone incentives, but no signed agreement is on record (statewide Oregon EZ moratorium eff. June 2026) -> subsidy honest-zero.

switch-big-beaver-pa.name: Big Beaver Campus
switch-big-beaver-pa.source: Switch announces new data center campus in Beaver County, Pennsylvania
switch-big-beaver-pa.notes: 382-acre campus, approximately 40 miles NW of Pittsburgh near the Ohio border.

powerhouse-pax-carlisle-pa.name: PAX — Pennsylvania Digital I
powerhouse-pax-carlisle-pa.developer: PowerHouse Data Centers / Pennsylvania Data Center Partners
powerhouse-pax-carlisle-pa.water_notes: Evaporative cooling for peak thermal conditions. A $14.1M agreement with the Middlesex Township Municipal Authority grants access to up to 400,000 gal/day (0.4 MGD) - a contracted ceiling (~2,367 dwelling units), not measured operational use; regulated by PA DEP and the Susquehanna River Basin Commission.
powerhouse-pax-carlisle-pa.nearest_nuclear_name: Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island Unit 1)
powerhouse-pax-carlisle-pa.source: Pennsylvania Data Center Partners and PowerHouse Data Centers launch JV to build 1.35 GW hyperscale campus in Carlisle
powerhouse-pax-carlisle-pa.notes: 'Pennsylvania Digital I' (PAX) in Carlisle, Cumberland County: a ~700-acre, three-campus development delivering 1.35 GW (expandable to 1.8 GW — in notes), each campus with six buildings and a 450 MW substation. The $15B is the project value across all three campuses (in notes). Near-term 300 MW by Q2 2027. Coordinates are the Carlisle area centroid. The $15B figure is the three-campus JV total, not broken out per campus -> investmentUsd omitted. Pennsylvania's data-center sales-tax exemption eligibility is likely but no confirmed award or LERTA designation was found.

stonebridge-powder-mills-lawrence-county.name: Powder Mills Data Center Campus
stonebridge-powder-mills-lawrence-county.source: Data center campus proposed at former dynamite factory site in Lawrence County, Pennsylvania
stonebridge-powder-mills-lawrence-county.notes: 569-acre parcel off Route 551 (3478 Howard Drive), split between North Beaver and Mahoning Townships; 16 data-center buildings plus an electrical substation; developer cites >$15B investment and 3,000-4,000 construction/permanent jobs. Site requires environmental remediation from prior explosives manufacturing.

meta-aiken-county-sc.name: Meta Aiken Data Center
meta-aiken-county-sc.source: Meta plans $800m data center campus in Aiken County, South Carolina
meta-aiken-county-sc.notes: Sage Mill Industrial Park, Graniteville. 715,000 sq ft; Meta's 22nd US data center. Explicitly optimized for AI workloads. Administration building constructed with mass timber. Expected operational spring 2027. Coordinates are Graniteville area centroid.

project-boulder-colleton-county-sc.name: Project Boulder
project-boulder-colleton-county-sc.source: Gigawatt data center proposal draws opposition from SC Lowcountry residents, politicians
project-boulder-colleton-county-sc.notes: Near the ACE Basin (Ashepoo-Combahee-Edisto estuary). Would be South Carolina's first gigawatt-scale data center if built; speculative, no named tenant. Coordinates are approximate.

edgeconnex-cedar-creek-tx.name: AUS02 / Cedar Creek Campus
edgeconnex-cedar-creek-tx.source: EdgeConneX plans second data center campus in Bastrop County
edgeconnex-cedar-creek-tx.notes: 4-building campus, approximately 140 acres near Wolf Ln/FM 535.

aligned-project-caprock-hale-county-tx.name: Aligned Data Centers Project Caprock
aligned-project-caprock-hale-county-tx.powered_by: Grid (Xcel Energy); dedicated electrical infrastructure funded by Aligned
aligned-project-caprock-hale-county-tx.water_notes: DeltaFlow liquid cooling technology with closed-loop air-cooled heat rejection; no Ogallala Aquifer water use per developer.
aligned-project-caprock-hale-county-tx.source: Aligned breaks ground on Project Caprock 540 MW campus in Hale County
aligned-project-caprock-hale-county-tx.notes: Six facilities totaling 1.65 million sq ft across 313 acres. Largest data center groundbreaking in West Texas at time of announcement. TeraWulf separately targeting a data center campus in Abernathy for Fluidstack. Coordinates corrected: Abernathy TX is at approximately 33.84°N, 101.84°W; original record had longitude −101.55 which is ~15 miles east of the city.

cipher-black-pearl-wink-tx.name: Cipher Black Pearl Campus
cipher-black-pearl-wink-tx.notes: ~300 gross MW HPC/AI campus near Wink, Winkler County, under a 15-year AWS lease; Phase I targeted Q4 2026. Cipher transitioning crypto → HPC/AI. Coordinates are the Wink area centroid. Cipher Mining (Nasdaq: CIFR) financed Black Pearl via ~$2.0B senior secured notes (Black Pearl Compute LLC, Feb 2026) plus a ~$232.5M equity reimbursement (~$2.23B implied total, inferred across two instruments) -> investmentUsd omitted; the ~$9.3-9.8B AWS figure is 15-year lease revenue, not capex. No jobs figures disclosed -> jobs honest-zero. Mining-era cooling was ~250 MW air-cooled + ~50 MW liquid-cooled; the HPC/AI cooling architecture is undisclosed -> water honest-zero. No confirmed public subsidy surfaced.

cipher-colchis-tom-green-tx.name: Cipher Colchis Campus
cipher-colchis-tom-green-tx.source: Cipher Digital Inc. FY2025 Form 10-K — Item 1 Site Pipeline, Colchis Site (1-GW West Texas, 620 acres, AEP Direct Connect, energize 2028)
cipher-colchis-tom-green-tx.notes: 1-GW HPC/AI development site in Tom Green County, northeast of San Angelo near AEP's Red Creek 345-kV substation (~2,500 ft east of the Skybox San Angelo campus). In November 2025 Cipher purchased a majority interest in a JV (Colchis LLC) to develop the site, with options to buy ~620 acres of land adjacent to the existing substation; Cipher expects ~95% equity subject to final lease/development terms. Coordinates are the NE-San-Angelo / Red Creek substation area centroid (approximate) pending a parcel-level GIS lookup. Investment and jobs figures undisclosed -> omitted. County pinned via local press (San Angelo LIVE); the SEC 10-K discloses only "West Texas."

cipher-mikeska-mcculloch-county-tx.name: Cipher Mikeska HPC Data Center
cipher-mikeska-mcculloch-county-tx.source: Cipher Digital (Cipher Mining) FY2025 Form 10-K — Mikeska Site, West Texas, targeted capacity up to 500 MW, energize 2028; option to purchase exercised Feb 2026
cipher-mikeska-mcculloch-county-tx.notes: Cipher's Mikeska HPC/AI data center site, in West Texas outside Brady (McCulloch County). Targeted capacity up to 500 MW; estimated energization 2027-2028. Cipher exercised its option to acquire the ground lease/purchase rights in February 2026. Part of Cipher's ~3.4 GW / 8-site HPC pipeline (Cipher Digital, formerly Cipher Mining). Coordinates approximate (Brady, TX geocode).

crusoe-blue-energy-victoria-tx.name: Crusoe Victoria AI Factory
crusoe-blue-energy-victoria-tx.powered_by: On-site generation (Blue Energy: gas bridge → nuclear)
crusoe-blue-energy-victoria-tx.source: Blue Energy and Crusoe partner to develop nuclear-powered AI data center
crusoe-blue-energy-victoria-tx.notes: Crusoe-developed AI factory campus at the Port of Victoria, powered by Blue Energy (natural-gas bridge as early as 2028, nuclear targeted ~2031). Distinct from Crusoe's Stargate Abilene campus. ~1.5 GW planned. Coordinates are the Victoria area centroid.

google-wilbarger-vernon-tx.name: Google Wilbarger County Campus
google-wilbarger-vernon-tx.source: A new data center in Wilbarger County, Texas
google-wilbarger-vernon-tx.notes: Air-cooled data center near Vernon, Wilbarger County — a Google/AES 'power-first' initiative. Part of Google's broader Texas expansion. IT capacity not disclosed. Coordinates are the Vernon area centroid.

meta-el-paso-tx.name: Meta El Paso AI Data Center Campus
meta-el-paso-tx.powered_by: Grid (El Paso Electric, renewable-matched); 366 MW McCloud gas plant proposed
meta-el-paso-tx.water_notes: Zero operational water use for most of the year via closed-loop liquid cooling. Commitment to restore 200% of consumed water to local watersheds by 2030.
meta-el-paso-tx.source: Meta breaks ground on El Paso AI-optimized data center
meta-el-paso-tx.notes: Campus located in far Northeast El Paso near Texas-New Mexico state line on approximately 1,000 acres; coordinates are approximate city-area centroid, exact parcel not publicly identified. Meta's third Texas data center. Campus can scale to 1 GW. Construction jobs figure (4,000) reflects updated peak estimate from March 2026 $10B expansion announcement.

stargate-milam-county-tx.name: Stargate Milam County Campus
stargate-milam-county-tx.water_notes: SB Energy states the facility uses a closed-loop water-cooling system 'designed to minimize water usage'; no permitted volume (MGD) is disclosed.
stargate-milam-county-tx.source: OpenAI Stargate: where the US sites stand — Epoch AI

tesla-cortex-2-giga-texas-austin-tx.name: Tesla Cortex 2.0 AI Training Cluster (Giga Texas)
tesla-cortex-2-giga-texas-austin-tx.source: Cortex 2.0: Tesla's new supercomputer at Giga Texas
tesla-cortex-2-giga-texas-austin-tx.notes: Dedicated, purpose-built AI training data center on the north side of Tesla's Giga Texas campus (unincorporated Travis County), separate from and adjacent to the original Cortex cluster. Trains neural networks for Full Self-Driving and the Optimus robot program; uses Nvidia GPUs. First ~250 MW targeted online with a full ~500 MW buildout targeted mid-2026; construction began early 2025. Coordinate is the Giga Texas campus point; Cortex 2.0 is a specific building on that campus.

meta-eagle-mountain-ut.name: Meta Eagle Mountain Data Center Campus
meta-eagle-mountain-ut.water_notes: Air-side economizer with evaporative assist and multi-pass water reuse. The campus consumed ~35.1 million gallons in 2024 (city data reported by Grist), more than double 2021. A 2018 confidentiality agreement kept monthly water use private and obliged the city to alert Meta to records requests, drawing transparency criticism. Meta pledges 200% water restoration by 2030 (e.g., a $200K Hobble Creek flow-restoration grant).
meta-eagle-mountain-ut.source: Meta Eagle Mountain Utah Campus — Baxtel

aws-birchwood-data-campus-king-george-va.name: Birchwood Data Campus
aws-birchwood-data-campus-king-george-va.developer: Amazon Web Services (via Birchwood Power Partners)
aws-birchwood-data-campus-king-george-va.location: King George, King George County, VA
aws-birchwood-data-campus-king-george-va.source: Virginia's King George County approves rezoning for AWS data campus
aws-birchwood-data-campus-king-george-va.notes: 869 acres (former power-plant site), 19 buildings, 7.5M sq ft; rezoning approved Sept 2023; contested vested-rights case in circuit court.

cloudhq-manassas-mcc-va.name: CloudHQ Manassas MCC Campus
cloudhq-manassas-mcc-va.water_notes: The first building (MCC1) uses a waterless air-side design — 152 Kyoto Cooling heat-wheel units driving PUE below 1.2; cooling for later buildings is not confirmed. The campus is within the Prince William Water service area.
cloudhq-manassas-mcc-va.notes: Seven-building campus; 382 MW total planned critical IT load; 96 MW currently available. Coordinates sourced directly from CloudHQ website (38.71955, -77.49819). Connects via Manassas Fiber Highway to CloudHQ's MDC campus.

green-energy-ventures-king-george-techno.name: King George Technology Center
green-energy-ventures-king-george-techno.location: King George, King George County, VA
green-energy-ventures-king-george-techno.source: Green Energy Ventures presents King George Technology Center
green-energy-ventures-king-george-techno.notes: 352 acres (40 already industrial-zoned) in the Route 3 West Settlement Area, bordering Stafford; rezoning pending.

microsoft-bristow-mnz03-va.name: Microsoft Bristow Data Center Campus (MNZ03)
microsoft-bristow-mnz03-va.water_notes: MNZ03 became operational around the 2024–25 transition in Microsoft's cooling standard (from evaporative-assist to closed-loop, zero-water evaporation for new designs), and the specific system installed here is unconfirmed. Microsoft reported reaching corporate 'water-positive' status in FY2025.
microsoft-bristow-mnz03-va.source: Microsoft 8008 Devlin Rd Data Center — Datacentermap.com
microsoft-bristow-mnz03-va.notes: Microsoft does not publicly disclose data center locations; sourced from public property records and third-party tracking databases. 8008 Devlin Road, Bristow. Adjacent to Amazon's Devlin Technology Park parcel and within Prince William County's Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District. Coordinates approximate. Status updated to operational per Baxtel (year built 2025); datacentermap.com returned HTTP 429 during fact-check and could not be independently read.

powerhouse-95-spotsylvania-va.name: PowerHouse 95
powerhouse-95-spotsylvania-va.developer: PowerHouse Data Centers (American Real Estate Partners / AREP, joint venture with Harrison Street)
powerhouse-95-spotsylvania-va.water_notes: Press materials do not disclose cooling approach for PH 95 specifically. PowerHouse has deployed direct-to-chip and closed-loop cooling at other campuses; no water draw figures available.
powerhouse-95-spotsylvania-va.source: PowerHouse breaks ground on 800MW data center campus in Spotsylvania County, Virginia
powerhouse-95-spotsylvania-va.notes: Campus located at approximately 4189 Turner Ct, Spotsylvania County, VA along the I-95/Hwy 17 corridor; coordinates are approximate. Three 300 MW substations planned (800 MW total); first substation delivering 150 MW targeted for Q4 2025. Up to 8 buildings, 3.5 million sq ft. Phased delivery Q3 2025–Q4 2027. Joint venture between PowerHouse/AREP and Harrison Street. Harrison Street managing director explicitly cited 'high-powered computing, AI, and other advancements' as the demand driver for this campus class, supporting likely AI classification. Named tenant not disclosed. Dominion Energy utility attribution is inferred from service territory: Dominion's Tributary 230 kV project was approved by Virginia SCC (June 30, 2024) specifically to serve growing Spotsylvania data center demand; PH95 press materials do not name the utility directly. Investment amount, job figures, and water draw not disclosed in any sourced press materials.

microsoft-mount-pleasant-wi.name: Microsoft Mount Pleasant Data Center Campus
microsoft-mount-pleasant-wi.water_notes: Primarily dry cooling with evaporative backup only above ~85°F, running waterless for 90%+ of the year. 0.702 MGD is the regulatory-filing peak for the full campus (Phase 1 peak ~0.234 MGD); water is sourced from the city of Racine (Lake Michigan).
microsoft-mount-pleasant-wi.source: Microsoft will invest $80B to build out AI infrastructure — Microsoft On the Issues

stargate-port-washington-wi.name: Stargate Lighthouse Campus
stargate-port-washington-wi.water_notes: Closed-loop liquid cooling using minimal water; Vantage commits to 'water positivity,' restoring more water than the campus consumes.
stargate-port-washington-wi.source: OpenAI, Oracle, and Vantage Data Centers Announce Stargate Site in Wisconsin — Vantage

pch-wi-holdings-wisconsin-rapids-wood-co.name: Wisconsin Rapids Data Center
pch-wi-holdings-wisconsin-rapids-wood-co.source: Who is the developer of the proposed Wisconsin Rapids data center?
pch-wi-holdings-wisconsin-rapids-wood-co.notes: 950 Fourth Ave N, former paper mill site. Developer reportedly affiliated with PNK Group USA. Conditional use permit application filed with the city April 30, 2026. Scale/investment not yet disclosed. Coordinates are approximate.

nscale-monarch-mason-county-wv.name: Monarch Compute Campus
nscale-monarch-mason-county-wv.source: Nscale and Microsoft Announce Collaboration with NVIDIA and Caterpillar to Deliver 1.35GW NVIDIA Vera Rubin at WV AI Factory Campus
nscale-monarch-mason-county-wv.notes: Nscale backed by $2B NVIDIA investment. Microsoft LOI covers 430,000 Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs in multi-year framework agreement. 8 GW ceiling for full site; capacityMw.planned reflects 2028 phase target of 2 GW. Acquired from AIPCorp (Fidelis New Energy / 8090 Industries). Coordinates are approximate for north of Point Pleasant, Mason County.
